WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:3 "so that no one would be disturbed by these afflictions"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:3 "so that no one would be disturbed by these afflictions" This is the only use of the term "disturbed" in the NT (or LXX).

  1. It originally referred to a dog wagging its tail.
  2. In classical Greek (Homer), it was used in the sense of "flattered."
  3. This may relate to 1 Thess. 2:1 or 3:5 (i.e. "in vain")
  4. True faith perseveres (cf. Matt. 13:1-23; John 15:1-6; Gal. 6:9; Rev. 2:2-3,7,11,17,19,26; 3:5,8,10,11,12,21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE NEED TO PERSEVERE

▣ "we have been destined for this" This is a PRESENT PASSIVE (deponent) INDICATIVE. The PASSIVE VOICE implies that God is the active agent. It is not a reference to

  1. the pagan idea of an impersonal fate
  2. the Islamic idea of determinism

Suffering is the norm for believers in a fallen world (cf. 1 Thess. 3:3-4; Matt. 5:10-12; John 15:18, 20; 16:33; Acts 14:22; Rom. 8:17; 2 Cor. 4:7-11; 11:23-27; 2 Tim. 3:12; 1 Pet. 2:21; 4:12-16). Suffering is often a means toward spiritual maturity (cf. Heb. 5:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO CHRISTIANS SUFFER?

SPECIAL TOPIC: A SUFFERING MESSIAH

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:4 "we kept telling you in advance"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:4 "we kept telling you in advance" This is an IMPERFECT TENSE which means repeated action in past time. Paul must have warned them several times about the persecution and suffering connected to the gospel. He knew this from Jesus' teachings (cf. Matt. 5:10-12; John 15:20; 2 Tim. 3:12) and personal experience (cf. 2 Cor. 4:7-11; 6:3-10; 11:23-29). They now know it experientially also.

NASB  "we were going to suffer afflictions"
NKJV  "we would suffer tribulation"
NRSV  "we were to suffer persecutions"
TEV  "that we were going to be persecuted"
NJB  "we must expect to have persecutions to bear"

This is a PRESENT ACTIVE INDICATIVE with a PRESENT PASSIVE INFINITIVE. The Williams' translation footnote says "a picture of a loaded wagon crushed under its heavy load." I really like the Williams translation of the NT. I have put its website on the homepage of my website (www.freebiblecommentary.org).

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:5 "your faith"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:5 "your faith" This is possibly used in the OT sense of "faithfulness." Remember, the authors of the NT were Hebrew thinkers (except Luke) so the best place to consult the word meaning is the Koine Greek translation of the OT, done about 150 B.C. Were they true to their profession of faith?

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FAITH

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

▣ "the tempter might have tempted you" A personal, evil force (ho peirazōn) is active in our world and in our lives (cf. 1 Thess. 2:18). This Greek word translated "tempt" (peirazō) connotes tempting "with a view toward destruction," the opposite of "approved" (dokimazō) in 1 Thess. 2:4.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSONAL EVIL

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK TERMS FOR TESTING AND THEIR CONNOTATIONS

▣ "our labor would be in vain" The use of MOODS is important here; the INDICATIVE which is the MOOD of reality is used of Satan, but the SUBJUNCTIVE which is the MOOD of contingency, is used of Paul's labor. This may relate to 1 Thess. 2:1. The question is, "Does ‘in vain‘ relate to their personal conversion or the establishment of a viable functioning church in Thessalonica?" I think the latter is the only contextual option, although Paul probably would not have made a distinction. He understood and preached both justification and sanctification.

Paul uses the concept of "vain" or "fruitless" often and incorporates three different words.

  1. eikē ‒ Rom. 13:4; 1 Cor. 15:2; Gal. 3:4; 4:11; Col. 2:18
  2. kenos ‒ 1 Cor. 15:10,14,58; 2 Cor. 6:1; Gal. 2:2; Eph. 5:6; Phil. 2:16; Col. 2:8; 1 Thess. 2:1; 3:3 (VERB in 2 Cor. 9:3)
  3. matalos ‒ 1 Cor. 3:20; 15:17; Titus 3:9 (VERB in Rom. 2:21)

Paul knew the power of the gospel was from divine activity, but he also knew the choices of humans affected the effective outcome (i.e. John 15:1-6)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERAMCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:6 "good news"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:6 "good news" This is the only use of this Greek term in the NT where it does not refer to the gospel of Christ. Timothy's message about the faithful condition of this church was "gospel," "good news" to Paul.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

▣ "of your faith and love" This phrase can have several meanings (cf. 1 Thess. 1:3). This refers either to:

  1. orthodox doctrine and loving care for one another
  2. faithfulness and love toward God

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FAITH

▣ "think kindly of us, longing to see us just as we also long to see you" This shows that neither the pagan or Jewish persecution had embittered this church against Paul.

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:7 "in all our distress and affliction"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:7 "in all our distress and affliction" Paul's problems in Corinth are listed in 1 Cor. 4:9-13; 2 Cor. 4:7-12; 6:4-10 and 11:23-28. Oh my! The costs of being a servant of Christ and a church of Christ!!

▣ "we were comforted" Paul uses this compound word ("with" and "call") often. It has several senses.

  1. to urge, exhort, encourage (cf. 1 Thess. 2:3,11; 4:1; 5:14; 2 Thess. 3:12)
  2. to comfort (cf. 1 Thess. 2:11; 3:2; 4:18; 5:11; 2 Thess. 2:17)
  3. its NOUN form (paraclētos) used of both the helping ministry of
    1. the Spirit (cf. John 14:16,26; 15:26; 16:7)
    2. the Son (cf. 1 John 2:1)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COMFORT

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:8 "for now we really live"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:8 "for now we really live" Paul is using emotional imagery to express his release from his deep concern because of the good news about this church.

▣ "if you stand firm in the Lord" This is a Greek CONDITIONAL SENTENCE, combining FIRST CLASS and THIRD CLASS conditions, thereby adding contingency to Paul's statement. He assumed that they would stand firm but that remained for him to see (cf. 1 Thess. 2:1 and 3:5).

"Standing firm" relates to our position in Christ. The Bible presents our salvation in a tension-filled pair of truths:

  1. it is free, it is in Christ
  2. it is costly, it is progressive, it is seen in our lifestyle choices (Matthew 7; John 15; James, 1 John)

Both are true. This verse emphasizes the first truth (cf. Rom. 5:2; 1 Cor. 15:1 and Eph. 6:11, 13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: STAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY

▣ "Lord" See SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (adon and kurios)

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:9-10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 3:9-10 This is a rhetorical question that leads into a prayer, 1 Thess. 3:11-13, concluding the first half of Paul's letter.

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:10 "night and day"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:10 "night and day" This is the Jewish order of time (see note at 1 Thess. 2:9). This reflects Paul's constant, persistent prayer life (cf. 1 Thess. 1:2; 2:12; 2 Tim. 1:3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: EFFECTIVE PRAYER

NASB  "keep praying most earnestly"
NKJV  "praying exceedingly"
NRSV  "we pray most earnestly"
TEV  "we ask him with all our heart"
NJB  "We are earnestly praying"
Peshitta  "offer supplication abundantly"

The ADVERB "most earnestly" is a very strong, triple compound (huper + ek + perissou). It is a highly emotional term (cf. Eph. 3:20; 1 Thess. 3:10; 5:13). Paul constantly worried and prayed about these new churches (cf. 2 Cor. 11:28).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S USE OF HUPER COMPOUNDS

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

NASB, Peshitta  "may complete what is lacking in your faith"
NKJV  "perfect what is lacking in your faith"
NRSV  "restore whatever is lacking in your faith"
TEV  "supply what is needed in your faith"
NJB  "make up any shortcomings in your faith"

They had done well but they were not yet mature in their understanding, as the misunderstanding about the Second Coming shows. This is the use of "faith"

  1. as doctrine (cf. 1 Thess. 4:13-5:11)
  2. the recurrent emphasis on lifestyle, "what was lacking" may have had an ethical aspect (cf. 1 Thess. 4:1-12)

Paul uses this term faith (pistis/pisteuō) often in these letters (cf. 1 Thess. 1:3,8; 3:2,5,6,7,10; 5:8; 2 Thess. 1:3,4,11; 3:2), but especially in this context.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH, BELIEVE, OR TRUST

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FAITH

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:11 "may. . .direct"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:11 "may. . .direct" This is a rare AORIST ACTIVE SINGULAR OPTATIVE VERB, used in several prayers in the NT (cf. 1 Thess. 5:23; 2 Thess. 2:16; 3:5, 16 and in Rom. 15:5-6,13). Note the VERB is SINGULAR, though it refers to both God the Father and Jesus Christ. This was a way for the NT authors to assert the Deity of Jesus of Nazareth (cf. 1 Thess. 1:1; 2 Thess. 2:16; also note Matt. 28:19).

Another theological point is that just as Satan prevented Paul from coming to them, recorded in 1 Thess. 2:18, Paul asked the Father and Son to make a way (straight or smooth: cf. Luke 1:79) for him to visit them!

▣ "Father" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHERHOOD OF GOD

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:11-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:11-13 This is one sentence in Greek. This prayer contains three rare OPTATIVE VERBAL forms:

  1. "direct" (1 Thess. 3:11)
  2. "increase" (v. 12)
  3. "abound" (v. 12)

The OPTATIVE MOOD is the MOOD of potentiality used in prayers.

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:12 "abound"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:12 "abound" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOUND (perisseuō)

▣ "for all people" God's love is as wide as the world (cf. John 1:29; 3:16; 4:42; 12:47; Rom. 5:18; 1 Tim. 2:4; Titus 2:11; 3:4; Heb. 2:9; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:2; 4:14); so too, must be ours who know Him.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:12-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:12-13 Paul prayed for himself in 1 Thess. 3:11 (he asked for prayer in Eph. 6:19), but now his petition turns toward the church at Thessalonica.

  1. He prayed for their love for one another and all people (cf. Eph. 6:18).
  2. He also prayed for the believers' holiness (cf. 1 Thess. 3:13; Eph. 1:4). God's will for every believer is Christlikeness (cf. Rom. 8:28-29; 2 Cor. 3:18; 7:1; Gal. 4:19; Eph. 1:4; 4:13; 1 Thess. 4:3,7; 5:23; 1 Pet. 1:15).

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 3:13 "hearts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:13 "hearts" See SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

NASB  "without blame in holiness"
NKJV, Peshitta  "blameless in holiness"
NRSV, NJB  "in holiness that you may be blameless"
TEV  "perfect and holy"
REB  "holy and faultless"

Holiness is both a gift and a task (INDICATIVE and IMPERATIVE). The word "blameless" is characteristic of someone above reproach, against whom no accusation may be brought (cf. Eph. 5:27). This leaves Satan with no basis for criticism (cf. Rom. 8:31,32,33). God's will for every believer is Christlike holiness (cf. 1 Thess. 4:3; Rom. 8:28-29; Gal. 4:19; Eph. 1:4). See note at 2 Thess. 4:3.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLAMELESS, INNOCENT, GUILTLESS, WITHOUT REPROACH

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

▣ "at the coming of our Lord Jesus" This shows Paul's continuing concern about end-time events (cf. 1 Thess. 2:19; 4:15-17).

The exact relationship between the events of

  1. the Second Coming
  2. the Rapture (cf. 1 Thess. 4:13-18)
  3. the Judgment Seat of Christ (cf. 2 Cor. 5:10)
  4. the White Throne of Judgment (cf. Matthew 25 and Revelation 20)

are uncertain. Be careful of dogmatism in this area. I think they are all simultaneous!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SECOND COMING

SPECIAL TOPIC: RAPTURE

▣ "His saints" "Saints" (lit. "holy ones") are either (1) angels who will accompany Jesus (cf. Deut. 33:2-3; Zech. 14:5; Matt. 16:27; 25:31; Mark 8:38; 2 Thess. 1:7; Rev. 19:4); or (2) His people, saints (cf. 1 Thess. 4:14-16). Paul never called angels "saints" or "holy ones," possibly solving the interpretive issue. Probably both angels and saints will return with Him on the clouds of heaven. This church was unsure if the dead saints would participate in the end-time events.

Saints, literally "holy ones," are called to holiness (cf. 1 Thess. 4:3) by the Holy One (cf. 1 Pet. 1:15)! The goal of Christianity is "holiness" now (cf. Eph. 1:4), not heaven when we die!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

SPECIAL TOPIC: SAINTS

SPECIAL TOPIC: GODLY ONES

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

▣ Some Greek MSS add "Amen" (i.e. MSS אi*2, A, D*), but other very early ones omit it (i.e. MSS אi1, B, D2, F, G). The UBS4 is uncertain about its inclusion, but Bruce Metzger (i.e. A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament, p. 631) thinks it was left off because scribes thought an "Amen" in the middle of a letter was inappropriate.

▣ "Amen" See SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why was it hard for Paul to be alone?
  2. List the different meanings of the term "faith."
  3. Is suffering normal for believers? Why?
  4. Is sanctification initial or progressive?
  5. Does verse 5 refer to one's salvation or fruitfulness? How do 2:1 and 3:5 relate to the parable of the Soils (cf. Matt. 13:1-23)?

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:1 "Finally then"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:1 "Finally then" This is literally "for the rest." This possibly begins Paul's practical section. Most of Paul's letters can be divided into a doctrinal section and a practical section although it is hard to do this in 1 Thessalonians. Paul often used this phrase to introduce the last major subject, not as an immediate prelude to a closing (e.g. 2 Cor. 13:11; Eph. 6:10; 2 Thess. 3:1).

▣ "brethren" Paul often uses this term (cf. 1 Thess. 1:4; 2:1,9,14,17; 3:7; 4:1,10,13; 5:1,4,12, 14,25,26,27; 2 Thess. 1:3; 2:1,13,15; 3:1,6,13). This is obviously a generic reference to all believers.

  1. to start a new subject
  2. to endear himself to his readers/listeners

▣ "request and exhort" Paul uses these PRESENT ACTIVE INDICATIVES to emphasize continuing action and to soften his commands as an Apostle (cf. 1 Thess. 4:2,11; 2 Thess. 3:4,6,10,12).

▣ "as you received from us instruction" This is an AORIST ACTIVE INDICATIVE, which points to the time Paul was with them personally. This is the Greek term that means "receive traditional teachings from another" (cf. 1 Thess. 2:13; 2 Thess. 2:15; 3:6; 1 Cor. 11:2,23; 15:1; Gal. 1:9; Phil. 4:9). Paul not only taught them how to be saved (justification), but also how to live as saved people (sanctification). Justification must never be separated from sanctification! Never!

▣ "as to how you ought to walk" This is a PRESENT INFINITIVE. Walk is biblical imagery for daily lifestyle faith (cf. 1 Thess. 2:12; Eph. 2:10; 4:1,17; 5:2,15; Col. 1:10; 2:6). Christianity was originally called "The Way" (cf. Acts 9:2; 19:9,23; 22:4; 24:14,22; 18:25-26). This speaks of an abiding lifestyle faith. Our initial response in repentance and faith must be followed by continuing repentance, faith, obedience, and perseverance. Eternal life has observable characteristics! In Christ every day is sacred, special, and used for worship and ministry.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "and please God" God's will for His children is not heaven when they die only, but Christlikeness now (cf. Rom. 8:28-29; 2 Cor. 3:18; 7:1; Gal. 4:19; Eph. 1:4; 2:10; 4:13; 1 Thess. 3:13; 4:7; 5:23; 1 Pet. 1:15). God wants a people who reflect His character to a lost and needy world!

NASB  "(just as you actually do walk)"
NKJV     —omitted—
NRSV  "(as, in fact, you are doing)"
TEV  "This is, of course, the way you have been living"
NJB  "as you are already living it"
REB  "you are indeed already following it"

A Greek manuscript problem is connected to this phrase. This phrase is missing in the Greek uncial manuscripts Dc, K, L, and the Textus Receptus texts. It is present in MSS א, A, B, D*, F, G and also in the Syriac, Coptic, and Vulgate translations. It is surprising that the early manuscripts have it and the later ones omit it. This implies that it was dropped out accidently. The UBS4 rates its inclusion as "A" (certain).

This is either PRESENT INDICATIVE or IMPERATIVE MOOD. It is probably INDICATIVE in that it asserts Paul's confidence in their Christlike lifestyle (cf. NASB, NRSV, TEV, and JB).

▣ "that you excel still more" They were doing well, but Paul urged them on to even greater holiness (cf. 1 Thess. 4:10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOUND (perisseuō)

4:2
NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "commandments"
NRSV, NJB, TEV  "instructions"
REB  "rules"

This is a rare military word for authoritative commands handed down through the ranks (cf. 1 Tim. 1:5, 18). I have included my Special Topic on the use of this word in John that parallels Paul's usage. The New Covenant does have requirements (i.e. Matt. 11:29, rabbinical use of "yoke"). I would denote the requirements of Jesus as

  1. need to repent (initially and continuously; see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [NT])
  2. need for faith (initially and continuously; see SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH, BELIEVE, OR TRUST)
  3. obedience (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)
  4. service
  5. love for the Triune God and His people (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVE)
  6. worship (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)
  7. Christlikeness (see SPECIAL TOPIC: NT EVIDENCE OF ONE'S SALVATION)

SPECIAL TOPIC: "COMMANDMENT" IN JOHN'S WRITINGS

▣ "by the authority of the Lord Jesus" These were not Paul's personal thoughts but Jesus' teachings. Paul's Apostolic authority rested on Jesus' authority (cf. 1 Thess. 4:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRIST JESUS AS LORD

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

EXPANDED OUTLINE OF 1 Thessalonians 4:1-12

  1. Introductory remarks, 1 Thess. 4:1-2

  2. Warnings about sexual immorality, 1 Thess. 4:3-8. For more information see the list of the inappropriate actions and motives of Paul's opponents at 1 Thess. 1:5.
    1. be holy, 1 Thess. 4:3a
    2. practice abstinence from sexual immorality, 1 Thess. 4:3b
    3. be sexually self disciplined, 1 Thess. 4:4-5
    4. practice appropriate sexuality by not defrauding your covenant brother's sexual rights, 1 Thess. 4:6-8
      SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY)

  3. Exhortations to other Christians, 1 Thess. 4:9-12
    1. Christians are to love one another, 1 Thess. 4:9-10
    2. live better and better, 1 Thess. 4:10b
    3. live quiet lives, 1 Thess. 4:11a
    4. tend to your own affairs, 1 Thess. 4:11b
    5. do your own labor, 1 Thess. 4:11c
    6. so that you may be a witness to the lost, 1 Thess. 4:12

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:3 "For this is the will of God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:3 "For this is the will of God" There is no ARTICLE, therefore, this is one of God's wills (cf. Eph. 5:17), after salvation (cf. John 6:40).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WILL (thelēma) OF GOD

▣ "your sanctification" This word shares the same root word with "holy" and "saints." Sanctification, like justification, is an initial instantaneous act of grace (cf. 1 Cor. 1:2,30; 6:11). Positionally, believers are in Christ. However, it should develop into lifestyle character, progressive sanctification (cf. 1 Thess. 4:7; 3:13; Rom. 6:19-23). God's will for every Christian is Christlikeness!! We cannot separate justification from sanctification!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

▣ "abstain from sexual immorality" This is literally "fornication." Premarital and extramarital sex were distinguished in the OT by separate words, but this word's meaning was broader in scope in the NT. "Fornication" meant all inappropriate sexual activity, including homosexuality and bestiality. Often pagan worship included sexual activity (i.e. imitation magic, cf. 1 Thess. 5:22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOMOSEXUALITY

SPECIAL TOPIC: ADULTERY

4:4
NASB, NKJV  "to possess"
NRSV  "to control"
TEV  "how to take"
NJB  "to use"
Peshitta  "to keep"
REB  "to gain mastery over"

This is a PRESENT MIDDLE (deponent) INFINITIVE. It is literally "to continually acquire" or "to possess."

NASB, NKJV  "his own vessel"
NRSV  "your own body"
TEV  "a wife"
NJB  "the body that belongs to him"
Peshitta  "his possessions"
REB  "his body"

This can refer to "his own body" or "his own wife." Theodore of Mopsuestia, Augustine, rabbinical usage, 1 Pet. 3:7, and the Septuagint interpret this in the sense of "wife" (cf. TEV). But the early Church Fathers (i.e. Tertullian and Chrysostom) interpreted it as "body" and this fits the context best (cf. NRSV, JB, NIV). Vessel is used in the sense of "body" in 2 Cor. 4:7.

▣ "in sanctification and honor" Knowing Jesus changes the way one lives. Believers are stewards, dependent on another's will. God's will is to use every believer to show His transforming power to a lost world. Christian marriage is a powerful witness in a fallen confused world!

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:3-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 4:3-6 This is one sentence in Greek.

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:5 "not in lustful passion"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:5 "not in lustful passion" This refers to fallen mankind's inability to control themselves sexually (pagan worship). Sexuality is a gift of God (cf. Genesis 1-2), but like all of God's gifts, they are taken beyond God-given bounds by fallen humans.

Self-control is a characteristic of a Spirit filled, Spirit led life (cf. Gal. 5:23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

▣ "like the Gentiles" This is literally "the nations." The lifestyle of the pagans of Paul's day was very immoral.

▣ "who do not know God" This does not exclude "natural revelation" (cf. Ps. 19:1-6 and Romans 1-2), but speaks of personal knowledge (cf. Gal. 4:8-9). In the OT "know" can have the connotation of intimate, personal relationship (cf. Gen.4:1; Jer. 1:5). Gentiles are estranged from God (cf. Eph. 2:11-13; 5:8; Col. 1:21), but tragically, so are the Jews.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:6 "transgress"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:6 "transgress" This term means "to go beyond bounds."

▣ "defraud" This term means "to take advantage of." It is related to the term "greed."

▣ "his brother" This may relate to taking sexual liberties with another believer's family (cf. 1 Thess. 4:9). But the term "brother" in context could refer to any other human, similar to "neighbor" (cf. 1 Thess. 4:12).

False teachers are often characterized by

  1. sexual exploitation
  2. financial exploitation
  3. claims of special privilege and special revelations

▣ "in the matter" This has the DEFINITE ARTICLE and therefore refers to 1 Thess. 4:3-5 (i.e. sexual purity). The word itself refers to business affairs. Therefore, it could be used as imagery for

  1. sexual matters
  2. or Paul changes subjects in 1 Thess. 4:6 and is now dealing with financial issues
  3. I think the first option is best.

▣ "because the Lord is the avenger in all these things" This refers to even-handed justice—both temporal (cf. Rom. 1:24,26,28) and eschatological (cf. Matt. 25:31ff.). YHWH is an ethical God (cf. Gal. 6:7.) In 1 Thess. 4:6, 7a and 8a, three different reasons are given why the believers should live holy lives.

▣ "as we also told you before and solemnly warned you" This is a strong statement concerning sexual purity (cf. Heb. 13:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S USE OF HUPER COMPOUNDS

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:7 "God. . .called"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:7 "God. . .called" God always takes the initiative (cf. John 6:44,65) both in salvation (justification) and in the Christian life (sanctification).

This truth of the initiating sovereignty of our Creator God does not diminish His requirements of fallen mankind's repentant, faith response. Mankind's relationship with God is characterized by a turning "from" (repentance) and a turning "to" (faith). God has chosen to deal with fallen mankind by means of covenant. A good example of the dual aspect can be illustrated from Phil. 2:12-13!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALLED

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "sanctification" See note at v. 3.

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:8 "he who rejects this is not rejecting man but the God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:8 "he who rejects this is not rejecting man but the God" This is literally "treat as of little value." Paul asserts that along with the truth of the gospel goes the lifestyle imperatives. These are God's truths, not Paul's, 1 Thess. 2:13; 3:1-2. Godly lives do not commend us to God, but that is the only path after meeting Him in Christ (i.e. Eph. 2:8-9,10).

▣ "who gives His Holy Spirit to you" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE PARTICIPLE. There was a major fight in the early church over who sent the Spirit.

  1. the Father
  2. the Son
  3. both

This refers to the indwelling Spirit as both an initial and ongoing experience (i.e. Acts 2:38; 2 Cor. 1:22; 5:5; 1 John 3:24).

All three persons of the Trinity are involved in all the redemptive events. Believers are indwelt by

  1. the Spirit (cf. Rom. 8:9-10)
  2. the Son (cf. Matt. 28:20; Col. 1:27)
  3. the Father (cf. John 14:23)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT (gift of. . .)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

4:9
NASB  "love of the brethren"
NKJV, Peshitta  "brotherly love"
NRSV  "love of the brothers and sisters"
TEV  "love for your fellow believers"
NJB  "loving our brothers"

This is the Greek term, philadelphia. This refers to love for covenant partners (cf. Rom. 12:10; Heb. 13:1; 1 Pet. 1:23; 2 Pet. 1:7). The balancing statement about loving the lost is in 1 Thess. 4:12 (cf. 1 Thess. 3:12).

▣ "you have no need for anyone to write to you" This was Paul's tactful way of affirming them and yet encouraging them to greater effort (cf. 1 Thess. 4:10c). This does not refer to doctrinal matters (i.e. the Second Coming), but practical, ethical lifestyle.

This may reflect the New Covenant of Jer. 31:31-34.

▣ "for you yourselves are taught by God" This is PRESENT TENSE. The teaching continues as the indwelling Spirit continues (cf. 1 Thess. 5:1; John 14:26; 16:13; 2 Cor. 9:1; 1 John 2:20,27), which is a sign of the New Covenant (cf. Jer. 31:33-34).

The Greek term theodidaktoi (found only here in the NT) means "God taught" (cf. John 6:45) and its object is to "love one another" (cf. John 13:34; 15:12,17; 1 John 2:7-8; 3:11,23; 2 John 5). Love is the uncounterfeitable characteristic of YHWH (cf. 1 John 4:7-21)!

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:10 "you do practice"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:10 "you do practice" This is another PRESENT TENSE VERB which speaks of continuing action (cf. 1 Thess. 4:17). Paul affirms their love but challenges them to do even more (as he did their lifestyle purity in 1 Thess. 4:1).

▣ "to excel still more" They are doing a good job, but need to keep on even more (cf. 1 Thess. 4:1). Love is the unique signature of God (cf. 1 Corinthians 13). We never love enough (cf. 1 Thess. 3:12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOUND

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVE (agapē)

4:11
NASB  "to make it your ambition to lead a quiet life"
NKJV  "that you also aspire to lead a quiet life"
NRSV  "to aspire to live quietly"
TEV  "Make it your aim to live a quiet life"
NJB  "we do urge you, brothers, to go on making even greater
 progress and to make a point of living quietly"
Peshitta  "you endeavor to be quiet and to do your own business"

Verse 11 is a series of four PRESENT INFINITIVES used as IMPERATIVES, commanding continuing action. This is probably exhorting patience and normalcy in the excited atmosphere of the anticipation of the Second Coming (cf. 2 Thess. 3:10-12). "Stay ready and stay faithful," not "get ready," is the NT message in this area.

The term "ambition" means "consider as an honor" or "aspire." It is also used in Rom. 15:20 and 2 Cor. 5:9.

▣ "work with your hands" Remember the historical occasion for the writing was that some in the church misunderstood Paul's preaching on the Second Coming and had quit working, anticipating an immanent Christ's return (cf. 2 Thess. 2:1-4 and 3:6-15).

In Greek culture, manual labor was believed to be exclusively the work of a slave. But in Hebrew culture, everyone needed a vocation—a means of supporting themselves, even rabbis (cf. Acts 20:35; 1 Cor. 4:17).

Some early Greek uncial manuscripts, א*, A, D (NRSV), add "work with you own hand," but others (אi2, B, D*) omit it. UBS4 is uncertain whether it should be included ("C" rating).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SOON RETURN

SPECIAL TOPIC: SECOND COMING

▣ "just as we commanded you" This is a strong term for "order" (cf. 2 Thess. 3:4,6,10,12).

4:12
NASB, NRSV  "that you will behave properly toward outsiders"
NKJV  "that you may walk properly toward those who
  are outside"
TEV  "In this way you will win the respect of those who
  are not believers"
NJB  "so that you are seen to be respectable
  by those outside the Church"

People are watching. We are witnesses of God's transforming power (cf. Matt. 5:13-16; Col. 4:5; 1 Tim. 3:7; 5:14; 6:1; Titus 2:5). Eternal life has observable characteristics!

NASB  "not be in any need"
NKJV  "that you may lack nothing"
NRSV, Peshitta  "and be dependent on no one"
TEV  "and will not have to depend on anyone
  for what you need"
NJB  "though you do not have to depend on them"
REB  "and at the same time never be in want"

Apparently, the Christians who quit work were expecting the other Christians to provide all their needs. Believers are to use their resources for the needs of the Christian family (cf. 2 Cor. 8-9; Eph. 4:28), but not for those who refuse to work!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS TO 4:13-5:11

The context about the Second coming runs through 1 Thess. 5:11. Remember its focus is pastoral (cf. 1 Cor. 15:58). Doctrine is given, but only as it serves a godly lifestyle now!

I am amazed how many other eschatological events (usually from Daniel 9; 11) are assumed in this context (same is true of 1 Corinthians 15, esp. v. 58). Believers must be very careful of combining inspired texts in such a way as to give divine authority to human end-time schemes, systems, charts, and timelines.

In the area of eschatology, dogmatism and judgmentalism are always inappropriate. The church, from its very beginning, has not agreed on how to interpret or systematize the end-time events, people, nor a schedule/timeline!

Three small books from Zondervan that have helped me in this area of theology are:

  1. Four Views of the Book of Revelation (1998)
  2. Three Views on the Rapture (2010)
  3. Three Views on the Millennium (1999)

They allow each view to present itself and then the other view gets to show its weaknesses.

Another book that has been so helpful in interpreting prophecy and apocalyptic is D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SECOND COMING (chart)

SPECIAL TOPIC: RAPTURE

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:13 "we do not want you to be uninformed, brethren"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:13 "we do not want you to be uninformed, brethren" This is a common phrase in Paul's writings (cf. Rom. 1:13; 11:25; 1 Cor. 10:1; 12:1; 2 Cor. 1:8). Usually it introduced an important statement, similar to Jesus' use of "Amen, amen." Knowledge of Christian truth (doctrine and worldview) gives believers a stability in a fallen world. Thank God for a written revelation!

Paul uses several similar expressions to introduce important statements or truths.

  1. "I wish you to know that. . ." ‒ 1 Cor. 11:3; Col. 2:1
  2. "I make known to you brothers" ‒ 1 Cor. 15:1; 2 Cor. 8:1; Gal. 1:11
  3. "I want you to know brothers, that. . ." ‒ Phil. 1:12 (close to #1)

Paul desired that the believers fully understand the main points of the gospel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

▣ "brethren" This is the generic use of the term. See full note at 4:1.

▣ "about" Timothy probably communicated some questions from the Church concerning the Second Coming to Paul.

  1. What about the believers who had already died? Would they participate in the end-time events?
  2. Would believers be surprised by the Second Coming and thereby be unprepared for the end-time events?

Paul often uses this preposition "about" to introduce his answers to the Corinthian Church's questions (cf. 1 Cor. 7:1,25; 8:1; 12:1; also 1 Thess. 5:1).

NASB  "those who are asleep"
NKJV  "those who have fallen asleep"
NRSV, TEV, NJB  "those who have died"
Peshitta  "those who are dead"
REB  "those who sleep in death"

Greek manuscripts vary here.

  1. some uncial manuscripts have a PRESENT PARTICIPLE (i.e. "those who are sleeping"), א, A, B
  2. others have a PERFECT PARTICIPLE, such as D, F, G, K, and L (i.e. "those who have fallen asleep")
  3. scribes probably changed the original PRESENT to a PERFECT following the usage in Matt. 27:52 and 1 Cor. 15:20 (i.e. Metzger, p. 632)

Jesus used "sleep" as a euphemism for death.

  1. OT (cf. BDB 1011, i.e. 2 Sam. 7:12; 1 Kgs. 22:40; Acts 13:36
  2. NT: Matt. 27:52; John 11:11-14; Acts 7:60; 1 Cor. 7:39; 11:30; 15:6,18,20,51; 2 Pet. 3:4)
  3. the English term "cemetery" is derived from this Greek word

This does not refer to the doctrine of "soul sleep," that believers wait, unconscious, until Resurrection Day. The NT speaks of conscious, but limited fellowship after death (cf. Luke 16:19-31; 23:43; 2 Cor. 5:8; Phil. 1:23; Rev. 6:9) until Resurrection Day, the Second Coming, and the Rapture, which I believe all occur at one time.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

▣ "that you will not grieve as do the rest who have no hope" The VERB "grieve" is a PRESENT PASSIVE SUBJUNCTIVE (cf. Eph. 2:12). Believers must not continue to be grieved by physical death because we know the truths of the gospel.

  1. Jesus died for us (i.e. Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21)
  2. the Spirit who raised Him will raise us (Rom. 8:11; also note John 5:21)
  3. He is coming back for us (John 14:3; 1 Thess. 4:16-17)
  4. those who have died are already with Him (2 Cor. 5:6,8)

The pagan world (i.e. "the rest," cf. 1 Thess. 5:16) was at a loss for comfort at death. Socrates said, "Oh, that there were some divine word upon which we could more securely and less perilously sail, upon a stronger vessel."

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOPE

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:14 "if"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:14 "if" This is a FIRST CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE which is assumed true from the author's perspective or for his literary purposes.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS, VII

▣ "we believe" This is the important theological VERB (PRESENT ACTIVE INDICATIVE) for human's putting their faith in Christ. This is the Greek VERB pisteuō, which is translated into English by "faith," "trust," or "believe."

This personal trust is characterized in the NT by using all the common Greek VERB TENSES:

  1. AORIST (past simple act), Acts 15:11; Rom. 8:24; 2 Tim.1:9; Titus 3:5
  2. PRESENT (ongoing process), 1 Cor. 1:18; 15:2; 2 Cor. 2:15; 1 Thess. 4:14
  3. PERFECT (past action which has come to completion and abides as a state of being), Eph. 2:5,8
  4. FUTURE (in VERB TENSE or context), Rom. 5:9,10; 10:9; 13:11; 1 Cor. 3:15; Phil. 1:28; 1 Thess. 5:8-9; Heb. 1:14; 9:28

It is an initial decision, followed by lifestyle discipleship that will one day be consummated in an eternal body and face-to-face fellowship with the Triune God (cf. 1 John 3:2). The theological progression can be seen in Rom. 8:29-30, from election, to justification, to sanctification, to glorification.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS, I

▣ "that" This hoti clause (i.e. PURPOSE CLAUSE) gives doctrinal content to the gospel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH, BELIEVE, OR TRUST, E. #5

▣ "Jesus died and rose again" These are both AORIST ACTIVE INDICATIVES which reflect historical facts. These gospel truths are the basis for the believer's hope:

  1. vicarious substitutionary atonement (cf. Isaiah 53; Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21)
  2. bodily, physical, eternal resurrection (cf. 1 Thess. 1:10; 1 Corinthians 15)

SPECIAL: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

SPECIAL TOPIC: RESURRECTION

▣ "God will bring with Him" This is a difficult phrase because the VERB (agō) has such a wide semantic field (to bring, to lead, to lead away, to lead out, to go, to go away, etc.). Does it imply that

  1. the dead are with Jesus in heaven?
  2. the dead will be raised at Jesus' coming?

In context the PRONOUN refers to Jesus, at His second coming. The Thessalonian believers did not understand Paul's preaching about the Second Coming. They wanted to know if those of their church who had already died would participate in the end-time events. This is Paul's positive response. Not only will they participate, they will receive their new bodies first and will accompany Jesus on the clouds of heaven.

The NT is not clear about the state of believers between death and Resurrection Day. When this passage is compared to 2 Cor. 5:6,8, postulating a disembodied period becomes a logical necessity (see Dale Moody, The Word of Truth, pp. 499-502 and Millard Erickson, Christian Theology, 2nd ed., pp. 1179-1190). Believers are with the Lord, but as yet do not have their resurrection bodies.

The Bible does not give much information about the afterlife, probably because believers in their fallen state could not comprehend its elements. A good small book that does discuss what the Bible reveals on this issue is William Hendriksen, The Bible On the Life Hereafter.

This is the only place in the Bible the Rapture is revealed!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COMING ON THE CLOUDS

SPECIAL TOPIC: RAPTURE

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?, III

▣ "in Jesus" This form is found in v. 16 and 1 Cor. 15:18, but here the Greek text has "through Him." Both forms speak of the agency and intimacy between the risen Savior and His followers.

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:15 "For this we say to you by the word of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:15 "For this we say to you by the word of the Lord" Paul was not giving his personal opinion but was relating Jesus' teachings (cf. 1 Thess. 4:2; also note 1 Cor. 7:10), however, this particular saying of Jesus is unrecorded in the Gospels. It is uncertain if this refers to

  1. oral Christian tradition (cf. Acts 20:35)
  2. Jesus' sermons, like Matt. 24 or Mark 13 or Luke 21
  3. if this was part of Jesus' personal revelation to Paul while in Arabia, Gal. 1:12; 2:2; Eph. 3:3
  4. later, direct revelation like 2 Cor. 12:1,9

This phrase implies that Paul is stating something he had received, which means that his eschatological views were not uniquely his; he is passing on what he received. The problem is we moderns do not know the source of this revelation or how widespread it was known.

We need to be reminded that the NT contains only a selected portion of Jesus' acts and teachings (cf. John 20:30-31; 21:25). For a good brief discussion about this issue see Gordon Fee and Douglas Stuart, How To Read the Bible For All Its Worth, pp. 127-148; also note pp. 17-32.

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "we who are alive and remain until the coming
  of the Lord"
NRSV  "we who are alive, who are left until the coming
  of the Lord"
TEV  "we who are alive on the day the Lord comes"
NJB  "left alive until the Lord's coming"

The use of the PRONOUN "we" could mean

  1. Paul expected the Lord back during his lifetime (i.e. vv. 14,17; 1 Cor. 15:51-52; Phil. 3:20)
  2. the editorial use of we (Paul expected to be "raised," 1 Cor. 6:14; 2 Cor. 4:14)

This expectation of an "any-moment" return of the Lord is the privilege of every generation of believers, but the experience of only one. This does not imply that Paul was inaccurate which would question the faith assumption of inspiration.

This may also be just a literary technique because in 2 Thessalonians Paul asserts a delayed Second Coming as Jesus did in Matthew 24 (and parallels) and Peter in 2 Peter 3.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SOON RETURN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ANY-MOMENT RETURN OF JESUS vs. THE NOT YET

SPECIAL TOPIC: DELAYED SECOND COMING

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

NASB  "will not precede"
NKJV, NRSV  "will by no means precede"
TEV  "will not go ahead"
NJB, REB  "will not have any advantage"
Peshitta  "shall not overtake"

This is a strong DOUBLE NEGATIVE, "never—no, never." Those saints who have died will fully participate in all the end-time events as will the believers who are alive at the Second Coming.

The KJV's translation "prevent" is misleading. No human can prevent the Second Coming.

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:16 "the Lord Himself"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:16 "the Lord Himself" The Greek text emphasizes Jesus' personal return—not a surrogate (cf. John 5:25-28).

▣ "will descend from heaven" Jesus will leave the Father's presence a second time to retrieve the family of faith (cf. John 14:2-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

NASB, NKJV  "with a shout, with the voice of the archangel
  and with the trumpet of God"
NRSV  "with a cry of command, with the archangel's call
  and with the sound of God's trumpet"
TEV  "There will be the shout of command, the archangel's voice,
  the sound of God's trumpet"
NJB  "at the trumpet of God, the voice of the archangel
  will call out the command"

The question remains how many heavenly persons are related to these three parallel events. There is a shout (this word is found only here in the NT), a voice and a trumpet blast (Peshitta). The JB assumes all three are done by the archangel and then Jesus descends. Other translations imply the first "cry," "command" or "shout" is from Jesus and then the archangel calls for the trumpet blast.

Heaven is prepared for this event—it is on the calendar. The uncertainty of when and how the event will occur fades into insignificance with the knowledge of Who will be coming. Jesus is coming again to receive His own.

▣ "the archangel" No ARTICLE appears, thus, it should read "an archangel." Although Dan. 10:13; 12:1 imply several (also note Deut. 32:8 in the LXX and I Enoch), the Bible mentions only one: Michael (cf. Jude 9). He is the national angel of Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELIC LEVELS IN PAUL'S WRITINGS

▣ "trumpet" The sounding of trumpets was a cultural way of announcing the approach of royalty in the East (cf. Heb. 12:18-19). However, it also functions in other ways.

  1. divine judgment, Rev. 8:2; 11:15-19
  2. resurrection, 1 Cor. 15:52
  3. gathering of the elect by angels, Matt. 24:31

This was a very important means of communication in the OT, used for religious and military events (cf. Exod. 19:16; Isa. 27:13; Joel 2:1; Zeph. 1:16; Zech. 9:14; 1 Cor. 15:52).

Two types of trumpets appear in the OT:

  1. silver trumpets (cf. Num. 10:2,8-10; 31:6)
  2. the left horn of a ram called the shophar (cf. Exod. 19:16,19; 20:18; Lev. 25:9; Joshua 6).

It is possible that all three sounds (shout, voice, trumpet) refer to the sounds made by the angel because in Rev. 1:10; 4:1 the angel's voice is called a trumpet (cf. Rev. 1:10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HORNS USED BY ISRAEL

▣ "and the dead in Christ will rise first" This phrase causes confusion about where the dead go between their death and resurrection day. This verse implies that they will remain in the grave (cf. Matt. 27:52-53). However, 2 Cor. 5:6,8 implies that they are with the Lord. The solution may be in postulating a disembodied state. The physical body remains in the grave, the life force goes to be with the Lord. There are many unanswered questions here. The Bible does not provide a clear teaching passage on this subject. See William Hendricksen, The Bible On the Life Hereafter.

Most translations translate it as if the saints are with God/Jesus and return with Him (cf. NASB). Another view is found in TEV, "Those who have died believing in Christ will rise to life first."

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?, III

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:17 "caught up"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:17 "caught up" Our theological concept of "rapture" originates from this VERB. "Rapture" is a Latin rendering of the Greek VERB here (harpazō – FUTURE PASSIVE INDICATIVE), which implies a forceful "snatching away" (cf. John 6:15; 10:12, 28-29). 1 Cor. 15:51-52 also discusses Christians, alive and dead, receiving their new bodies (cf. 1 John 3:2).

Many godly, sincere, prayerful, educated believers have disagreed about this end-time event. Some (i.e. particularly dispensationalists, but not me; see Dale Moody, The Word of Truth, pp. 555-557) expect a secret rapture of believers (cf. Matt. 24:40-42) before a thousand-year reign of Christ upon the earth. Often a seven year tribulation period (cf. Dan. 7:25; 9:27) is linked to this. Some theologians have the rapture before, in the middle, or after a seven year tribulation period. The order and nature of these end-time events are ambiguous at best. Dogmatism is surely inappropriate here. See my exegetical commentary on the book of Revelation online.

Believers are going to meet the Lord in the air, because in the NT the air was seen as the realm of Satan (cf. Eph. 2:2) and Greeks thought the lower air (atmosphere) was unclean and, therefore, the domain of unclean spirits. Believers will be reunited with their Lord in the midst of Satan's kingdom to show its complete overthrow.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SECOND COMING (chart)

SPECIAL TOPIC: RAPTURE

▣ "together with them" Alive and dead believers are united! This church had misunderstood Paul's preaching about the Second Coming. Paul wrote both 1 and 2 Thessalonians to answer these questions. The church wanted to know:

  1. Would the Christians who had died participate in these end-time events?
  2. When would dead and living believers be reunited?
  3. This subject is picked up in 2 Thess. 2:1.

▣ "in the clouds" Clouds are the traditional means of the transportation of Deity (cf. Dan. 7:13; Matt. 24:30; 26:64; Acts 1:9-11; Rev. 1:7). The image calls to remembrance the Shekinah cloud of the OT exodus experience (cf. Exod. 13:21,22; 14:19,20,24; 16:10; 19:9,16; 24:15,16,18; 34:5; 40:34-38) which symbolizes God's presence with His people.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COMING ON THE CLOUDS

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

▣ "to meet" This is the Greek word apanēsis, which is used in the sense of meeting someone and then accompanying them (cf. Matt. 25:6; Acts 28:15). So believers meet the Lord in the air and return to a recreated earth with Him (this is my current understanding)!

▣ "in the air" The air was considered the dominion of Satan and his followers by first century Judaism (cf. Eph. 2:2). We are going to meet the Lord there to show His complete victory. I think that while believers are united with Christ in the air, the prophecy of the cleansing and renewal of the earth in 2 Pet. 3:10 will occur. Heaven is depicted as a restored Garden of Eden (cf. Genesis 1-2 compared with Revelation 21-22).

▣ "we shall always be with the Lord" These Thessalonian believers will be united with their dead believing loved ones by Jesus Himself. Nothing further can be said (cf. Psalm 23:6). The Second Coming is referred to repeatedly in 1 Thessalonians (cf. 1 Thess. 1:10; 2:19; 3:13; 4:13-18; 5:1-11). Notice that neither in this book nor 2 Thessalonians does Paul mention (some see 1 Cor. 15:25 as a reference to an earthly reign) a thousand-year reign but an eternal reign, like Dan. 7:13-14.

Paul's terminology implies the eternal kingdom begins when Jesus returns. All of the other end-time events are simply not mentioned as in 1 Cor. 15:50-58. Paul does not even imply that Jesus returns completely to the earth. In Robert G. Clouses' The Meaning of the Millennium, all four major millennial positions are articulated by various authors. In the a-millennial response George E. Ladd makes this surprising statement, "I admit that the greatest difficulty to any pre-millennialism is the fact that most of the New Testament pictures the consummation as occurring at Jesus' parousia" (pp. 189-190). This is exactly what Paul is asserting here without any further elaboration.

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 4:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:18 This, like 1 Thess. 4:13, shows the purpose of Paul's presentation of these end-time events. The believers had many concerns about their fellow believers who had died. Would they be involved in the wonderful events of the Lord's return? Paul assured them that all believers, alive and dead, will be ultimately involved in the Second Coming (cf. Phil. 2:9-11).

Remember this passage is primarily pastoral (as is 1 Cor. 15:58), not didactic. How this fits into other eschatological passages is not clear. Also remember, this seems to refer to the eternal kingdom, (cf. Dan. 7:13,14), not a millennial reign (cf. Rev. 20:1-6; SPECIAL TOPIC: MILLENNIUM).

▣ "comfort" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Where in the Bible is the most detailed discussion of the Second Coming?
  2. What was the reason for Paul writing this passage?
  3. What is the Rapture? Who is involved? When will it occur?

entries.title: 1 Thessalonians 5:1 "Now as to"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:1 "Now as to" The subject of the Second Coming continues, but a new aspect of the event is approached: the judgment of unbelievers.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

NASB  "the times and the epochs"
NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta  "the times and the seasons"
TEV  "the times and occasions"
NJB  "times and seasons"
REB  "about dates and times"

Although believers are not to seek specific dates or times related to Jesus' return (cf. Matt. 24:36; Acts 1:7), they do need to recognize the trends of history (cf. Matt. 24:32-33).

  1. The Greek chronōn, translated "times," answers the question, "How long?" It speaks of the passing of time. The English word "chronology" is derived from this Greek root.
  2. Kairōn, translated "epochs," answers the question, "when?" It speaks of special events.

▣ "brethren" This is often used by Paul to mark a transition to a new subject (see 1 Thess. 4:1).

▣ "you have no need of anything to be written to you" Paul had not been able to give them extensive and prolonged information about the Second Coming. Remember, he only stayed a short time in Thessalonica, but he must have preached on this subject several times. This phrase does not mean to imply the Thessalonian believers perfectly understood all aspects of the end-time events but that the Spirit would lead them and inform them in the necessary areas (cf. John 14:26; 16:13; 1 John 2:20,27) especially those truths that relate to:

  1. the gospel
  2. the Christian life

The other possible option is that it refers to the New Covenant of Jer. 31:31-34, especially 1 Thess. 5:33-34. The New Age of righteousness is characterized by believers knowing God in intimate personal ways. They will not need a teacher for God has written His word on their hearts by means of the Spirit.
